The accused, Ng Sui-ting, appeared in court this morning wearing a green polo shirt, beige shorts, and a black face mask. The charges allege that the accused, on 10 July and 17 August respectively, allowed a male yellow mixed-breed dog to enter the vicinity of YOHO Mall in Yuen Long without being restrained on a leash no longer than two metres, facing two counts of 'allowing a large dog to enter or remain in a public place'.

The prosecution applied for the case to be adjourned for ten weeks before the next mention, and did not oppose the defendant's application for bail. Deputy Chief Magistrate Tang Siu-hung agreed to adjourn the case to 29 October for mention, and the defendant was granted bail.

Under the Dangerous Dogs Regulation, a conviction for 'allowing a large dog to enter or remain in a public place' carries a maximum fine of HK$25,000 and imprisonment for three months.

Assistant Director of the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department, Ip Yin, stated yesterday that if the dog owner decides to surrender the large dog to the government, the department will consider options including humane destruction; if the owner intends to reclaim the dog, the dog may be classified as a 'known dangerous dog', and the court may issue an order requiring it to wear a muzzle whenever it goes outside in future.

Kent, founder of the animal protection organisation毛守救援 (Mou Sou Rescue), said in an interview with集誌社 (Chickeeduck Art) that the dog owner regretted signing the abandonment form; he also stated that Mou Sou is willing to take in the dog and provide a canine trainer to assist with its rehabilitation.
